r0030: That provision was amended by Article 3 of Law no. 4793, which added a sixth ground for reopening:
r0031: “Where it has been established by a final judgment of the European Court of Human Rights that a criminal judgment was delivered in breach of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms and its additional Protocols. In such cases, the reopening of the proceedings may be requested within one year from the date on which the judgment of the European Court of Human Rights became final.”
r0032: Law no. 4793 came into force on 3 February 2003. Under its Provisional Article 1, Article 3 applies only in the following two situations: where the Court has delivered a judgment which became final before the entry into force of the Law; and where the Court delivers a final judgment concerning an application lodged after the entry into force of the Law.
r0034: I.  ALLEGED VIOLATION OF ARTICLE 6 OF THE CONVENTION
r0035: 13.  The applicant alleged that the State Security Court (*cour de sûreté de l'Etat*) which had tried and convicted him was not an “independent and impartial tribunal” capable of guaranteeing him a fair trial, on account of the presence of a military judge on the bench.
r0036: The applicant also complained that the proceedings before that court had been unfair. In that connection, he complained that he had not had the assistance of a lawyer while in police custody and that he had not had adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his defence.
r0037: He alleged a violation of Article 6 §§ 1 and 3 (b) and (c) of the Convention, the relevant parts of which provide:
r0038: “1.  In the determination of ... any criminal charge against him, everyone is entitled to a fair and public hearing ... by an independent and impartial tribunal ...
